title: Short Stuff: Third Man Syndrome
summary: Short Stuff episode on third man syndrome, the phenomenon in which people in extreme danger or exhaustion sense an unseen presence urging them on. The hosts cover Ernest Shackleton's 1914-1916 Antarctic expedition (ship crushed in sea ice, six-day row to Elephant Island, push to South Georgia Island with Worsley and Crean, who also reported the feeling), the origin of the term from T. S. Eliot's 1922 poem The Waste Land, John Geiger's 2008 book The Third Man Factor, Frank Smythe's 1933 Everest attempt, Joe Simpson's Touching the Void, the 9/11 survivors Ron DiFrancesco and Janelle Guzman McMillan, and a geologist cave diver who sensed her late husband. They close with theories, including Julian Jaynes's bicameral mind hypothesis and a hardwired instinct.

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Hosts joke that Jerry and Dave are the third and fourth men present, and tease the topic.

segments.title: Definition and Shackleton's expedition
segments.summary: Third man syndrome is defined as a sensed presence during extreme distress. Shackleton's 1914 expedition is described: ship crushed in ice, row to Elephant Island, then the push to South Georgia, where he felt an extra presence. Worsley and Crean reported the same feeling.

segments.title: Origin of the term and T. S. Eliot
segments.summary: Shackleton wrote about the experience in South (1919). The term is credited to T. S. Eliot's 1922 poem The Waste Land, which Eliot said was not inspired by a specific expedition. Hosts read the passage.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Brief transition before the list of cases.

segments.title: Historical and mountaineering cases
segments.summary: John Geiger's 2008 book The Third Man Factor collected stories. Frank Smythe's 1933 solo Everest attempt, where he offered food to his companion. Joe Simpson, who broke his leg in the Peruvian Andes in 1985 and followed a voice to safety (Touching the Void).

segments.title: 9/11 survivors and other known-person cases
segments.summary: Two 9/11 survivors reported the experience: Ron DiFrancesco, led down from the South Tower, and Janelle Guzman McMillan, trapped in the North Tower rubble, who called her presence a guardian angel named Paul. A geologist cave diver sensed her late husband.

segments.title: Explanations: instinct and bicameral mind
segments.summary: Scientists don't know the cause; it may be a hardwired instinct, and it is hard to study. Hosts connect it to Julian Jaynes's bicameral mind hypothesis, treating the presence as a vestigial part of the mind.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts wrap up and close the short episode, with the iHeartRadio production credit.
